title: Incomplete gamma at integer shape 2 to 20 is a stored polynomial of reciprocal factorials times EXP(-x)
statement: For an integer shape a from 2 to 20 and a < x <= 30, DNA Calc computes the upper tail as Q(a, x) = S(EXP(-x) * H), with H a Horner polynomial whose coefficients are 1/k! rounded once to binary64 (k = 0 to 19) and with every Horner multiply and add stored to binary64 before the next step; the result is EXP(-x) times the stored polynomial, and P = 1 - Q. The boundaries were located with adjacent-double probes: a == x and x > 30 do not take this route (they take the ordinary gamma-density route), and a divided Horner form, a forward term sum, and an extension to a >= 21 were each refuted. Over the full bank this matched 20 more rows net (3,889,422 to 3,889,442): CHIDIST +6, CHISQ.TEST +1, GAMMA.DIST +5, POISSON.DIST +3, GAMMA.INV +6 and -1, with four rows lost: CHIINV (0.001, 10), CHISQ.INV (0.6, 4) and (0.85, 4), GAMMA.INV (0.75, 5, 1); the first three are exact-inverse pins whose gains in the same functions offset them. On the oracle corpus the passed count went from 76,759 to 76,765. Measured and not taken: for large-mean POISSON, one stored product M*u*A gave +79 and -73, and M = RN64(V/D) resident into st(M*u) then st(T*A) gave +47 and -39 on the 542 large-mean POISSON misses, with gains and losses interleaved inside the same (k, mean) groups so no clean rule; a stored generic GAMMA seed fixes GAMMA(-0.5) and GAMMA(-1.5) but breaks GAMMA(-2.5), which matches today.
basis: Counts and boundaries are quoted from the DnaCalc commit message, code comments and bead comment (full-bank per-row traces); the two cited build 20131 rows are readings at integer shapes 2 and 3 inside the region, not a test of the polynomial's stores.
inferred: That Excel evaluates this polynomial with these coefficient loads and stores is inferred from the match and from adjacent-double probes; the coefficient loads are described in the code as conditional on the other loads and on EXP.
